title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text: The cohesion series reworks one of the oldest and most abused concepts in software design. Cohesion entered the field with Stevens, Myers, and Constantine in 1974 and was codified by Yourdon and Constantine. Five decades of research and measurement followed. This page collects what the cohesion series concludes.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 1 Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule
text:
1 Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule
The central definitional result: cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule.
A partitioning rule sorts the element set into equivalence classes — the elements that belong together. Against such a rule, a module deviates in exactly two ways:

Impurity. The module contains elements that belong to a different class.
Incompleteness. Some element of the module’s class resides outside the module.

So cohesion is assessed on two axes: purity and completeness. A module that is both pure and complete is fully cohesive: it holds exactly the elements its class requires, and nothing else.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 2 One pair per rule — the cohesion profile
text:
2 One pair per rule — the cohesion profile
A system is partitioned by many rules at once: logical code structure, deployment packaging, temporal grouping, security, platform. These are not separate things being partitioned. There is one element set EE, and each rule groups it by some of the change drivers acting on its elements.
For a system assessed under kk partitioning rules, cohesion is the 2k2k-tuple of (purity, completeness) pairs — one pair per rule. A module is fully cohesive when it scores maximally on every component.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 3 Structural proxies do not define cohesion
text:
3 Structural proxies do not define cohesion
The series argues that published definitions of cohesion overwhelmingly specify structural properties of code — method-call overlap, shared-field density, connected components.
These are not cohesion as defined by a modularization principle. They are structural proxies: observable patterns that correlate with cohesion but do not define it. A survey of 24 cohesion metrics spanning five decades shows that each measures structural coupling, not principled cohesion, reporting at most one axis and only as a proxy.
The distinction matters: a metric that counts structural overlap cannot detect the actual failure mode — whether a module holds elements the domain says belong elsewhere, or scatters the elements the domain says belong together.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 4 The Γ-equivalence rule is the coarsest change-containing partition
text:
4 The Γ-equivalence rule is the coarsest change-containing partition
Among all partitioning rules, one is special. Grouping elements by their full change-driver set — the Γ-equivalence rule — is the coarsest partition that still contains every change to one module.
Every modularization principle groups by a subset of the change drivers. Therefore every principle’s classes are unions of Γ-classes, and the Γ-decomposition is a refinement of every principle’s partition. A single Γ-decomposition is correct under all the principles at once.
This is the bridge from cohesion to the Independent Variation Principle: Γ-equivalence is the change-driver concretization of the general cohesion schema.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text:
5 The causal cohesion metric
When the partitioning rule is change-driver-assignment identity — elements belong together iff they share the same change-driver set — cohesion becomes causal cohesion.
For a single rule, causal cohesion is the two-dimensional metric
Hcausal(M)=(purity(M),completeness(M)) H_\text{causal}(M) = (\text{purity}(M), \text{completeness}(M)) 
in (0,1]×(0,1](0,1] \times (0,1]. It is one slot of the full cohesion profile, not the whole profile. Both axes are directly interpretable and map to design actions: low purity says separate elements of impure modules into distinct modules; low completeness says merge the scattered elements of a class into one module.
The metric satisfies the six necessary conditions the schema imposes on any admissible cohesion metric, and it has an operational computation procedure.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
section: 6 The four conditions are necessary and exhaustive
text:
6 The four conditions are necessary and exhaustive
Under the change-driver hypothesis and the objective of minimizing change propagation, four conditions are necessary and structurally exhaustive:

Admissibility — every element has at least one driver.
Element Form — every element is pure or irreducibly composite.
Separation — different-driver elements belong in different modules.
Unification — same-driver elements belong in the same module.

The first two constrain the element set; the last two constrain the partition. These are exactly the four conditions of IVP. The causal (purity, completeness) pair is the two-axis criterion these conditions reduce to when k=1k = 1.

title: Cohesion: Core Conclusions
text:
7 Where the proofs live
The derivations — that the four conditions are necessary and exhaustive, that Γ-equivalence is the unique minimizer, that the knowledge-embodiment theorem holds — are proved in the published cohesion papers: cohesion as correctness relative to a partitioning rule in the paper on the nature of cohesion [1], the four necessary and exhaustive conditions in the paper on cohesion and change propagation [2], and the causal cohesion metric in the paper on causal cohesion [3].
The knowledge-embodiment theorem — the result that maximal cohesion is maximal embodiment of domain knowledge — is treated on its own page.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text: This page covers a central result of the cohesion theory: the knowledge-embodiment theorem. It is placed here, under design, rather than under the IVP core theory, because it is a theorem about cohesion, not a theorem of IVP itself.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
1 Cohesion, briefly
Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule. Under any modularization principle that groups elements, a module has two properties:

Purity. The module contains no element from outside its correct class.
Completeness. The module contains every element of its correct class.

A module that is both pure and complete is maximally cohesive: it holds exactly the right elements and nothing else. When the partitioning rule is the change-driver rule, this recovers the IVP notion of maximal cohesion — but cohesion itself is the more general idea, defined for any rule, not only for IVP’s change-driver rule.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
2 The knowledge-embodiment theorem
The theorem connects this structural measure to an epistemic one.
cohesion(M)=(1,1)⇔Knowledge(M)=KP(Ci) \text{cohesion}(M) = (1, 1) \iff \text{Knowledge}(M) = K_P(C_i) 
A module has maximal cohesion under a rule PP if and only if it embodies exactly the knowledge its PP-class must hold — every knowledge piece its class requires, and no knowledge piece its class must not hold.
In words: maximal cohesion is maximal knowledge embodiment. Get the structure exactly right, and the module’s knowledge is exactly right, with no separate effort.
This is why the result lives in the cohesion theory. It is a statement about cohesion — it says what maximal cohesion means epistemically. IVP supplies one particular partitioning rule (the change-driver rule); the theorem itself is about cohesion in general.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
3 What maximal cohesion guarantees
A maximally cohesive module has four structural properties.

The module is epistemically self-contained. No knowledge its class must hold resides outside; no foreign knowledge resides inside.
The change radius is bounded. When a change driver governing the class’s knowledge activates, every affected element is in one module.
The module is independently verifiable. Correctness is checked against the class’s own knowledge, with no external consultation.
The module is independently replaceable. A replacement need only embody the same knowledge and answer to the same change drivers.

These are the structural conditions that underlie the benefits of modular programming under information hiding.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
4 What it does not guarantee
The phrase “maximal cohesion is correct embodiment” is easily over-read as “maximal cohesion is total correctness.” It is not.
A system has three distinct properties that this phrase blurs:

Placement — the right knowledge sits in the right modules. This is what cohesion measures.
Faithful embodiment — each piece present is realized correctly. This is functional correctness.
Dependency parsimony — the dependencies among elements are the ones the purpose requires.

These three are independent. A module can score maximal cohesion and be wrong (one element computes its piece incorrectly). A module can be maximally cohesive and faithful yet carry an unneeded dependency. A system can be entirely faithful and badly placed.
Cohesion governs the cost of achieving and maintaining correctness — the scope that must be read and the radius that must change — not whether the system is correct. A correct system may be incohesive and expensive to keep correct; a cohesive system may be incorrect and cheap to repair.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
text:
5 The knowledge floor
At maximal cohesion across all partition-inducing rules, every knowledge piece resides in exactly one module, and the system’s relevant causal domain knowledge is partitioned across exactly as many modules as there are classes. This is a theoretical lower bound on module count — a structural minimum, not a practical recommendation. Subdividing within a class for readability or team structure is freely available.

title: Cohesion and Knowledge Embodiment
section: 6 Where this sits in the theory
text:
6 Where this sits in the theory
The knowledge-embodiment theorem is proved in the published paper on the nature of cohesion [1], where cohesion is defined as correctness relative to a partitioning rule and the equivalence between maximal cohesion and maximal knowledge embodiment is established.
IVP and cohesion are related but distinct. IVP is the principle that groups elements by change-driver assignment. Cohesion is the more general measure of correctness relative to any partitioning rule. The change-driver rule is one instance of that general idea — the instance IVP is built on.

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
text:
Design dashboards like one number per module. Complexity, coupling, cohesion — a single score, a colour, a flag. This page shows why, for cohesion, one number cannot decide whether an element is well placed. The failure is not a matter of precision or of a poorly chosen formula. It is structural, and it has four independent causes.
A module can deviate from its rule in two opposite ways — it can hold elements that do not belong, or it can be missing elements that do. These two defects call for opposite repairs, and no single number can tell them apart. The rest of this page proves that claim and its companions.
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
text:
1 The setting
Cohesion is correctness relative to a partitioning rule [1]. A rule PP sorts the element set EE into equivalence classes [e]P[e]_P — the elements that belong together. A module M⊆EM \subseteq E complies when its boundary coincides with its class: M=[e]PM = [e]_P for every e∈Me \in M. Otherwise it deviates in one of two ways:

Impurity. MM contains elements from another class. The remedy is to remove them — to split.
Incompleteness. Some element of the module’s class lies outside MM. The remedy is to add it — to merge.

Assess a module MM against a class CC (the class it should realize). Write
purity(M)=|M∩C||M|,completeness(M)=|M∩C||C|.
\text{purity}(M) = \frac{|M \cap C|}{|M|},
\qquad
\text{completeness}(M) = \frac{|M \cap C|}{|C|}.

Both values lie in [0,1][0,1]. Purity is 11 exactly when MM has no foreign element; completeness is 11 exactly when MM is missing no member of CC. A module is fully cohesive precisely when both are 11.
The question of this page: can a single real number s(M)s(M) stand in for this pair and decide placement — issue the statement “this element is incorrectly placed”?
Two notions make the question precise.
Principled scalar. A function s(e,M,ℳ,E,R,P)→ℝs(e, M, \mathcal{M}, E, R, P) \to \mathbb{R} that may consult the principle PP as well as the structure — but whose output is one real number.
Verdict-deciding. ss decides placement iff there is an interpretation d:ℝ→{correct,incorrect}d: \mathbb{R} \to \{\text{correct}, \text{incorrect}\} with d(s(e,M))=VP(e,M)d(s(e,M)) = V_P(e,M) for every system and every element-module pair. (The module-level form s(M)s(M) is read the same way; the verdict is uniform across a module, so s(M)s(M) assigns one verdict to every element of MM.)
Four failure modes follow. They run from the strongest restriction on the metric — it cannot even see the rule — to the weakest — it sees everything and still adds nothing.

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 2 Failure mode 1 — the metric cannot see the rule
text:
2 Failure mode 1 — the metric cannot see the rule
Suppose the number is computed from the structure alone: from EE, RR, and the module MM, with no access to PP. Then it cannot decide placement, whatever its formula and whatever its precision.
Example. Let E={a,b}E = \{a, b\} and R=∅R = \emptyset, and let the module under test be M={a}M = \{a\}.

Under P1P_1 with a single class {a,b}\{a, b\}, we have [a]P1={a,b}≠M[a]_{P_1} = \{a,b\} \neq M, so aa is incorrectly placed (the module is missing bb).
Under P2P_2 with classes {a},{b}\{a\}, \{b\}, we have [a]P2={a}=M[a]_{P_2} = \{a\} = M, so aa is correctly placed.

The two systems present identical structural inputs — same EE, same RR, same MM — to any structural function, so such a function returns the same number for both. Yet the verdicts differ. No formula over the structure alone can be correct on both, at any level of precision.
This is the principle-blindness obstruction: the structure (E,R)(E,R) underdetermines PP, so “correct” — which is meaningless without PP — cannot be read off it. The constructive cell is also visible: give the metric access to PP and it can compare MM with [e]P[e]_P. But access alone is not enough, as the next three results show.
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 3 Failure mode 2 — one axis collapses two opposite defects
text:
3 Failure mode 2 — one axis collapses two opposite defects
Grant the metric full access to PP, but let it return one number per module, built from the two-axis pair: s(M)=g(purity(M),completeness(M))s(M) = g(\text{purity}(M), \text{completeness}(M)) for some g:[0,1]2→ℝg: [0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}.

Proposition (aggregation ambiguity). (a) If gg is symmetric — g(p,c)=g(c,p)g(p,c) = g(c,p) — there are two modules with opposite defects and opposite remedies whose scores are exactly equal. (b) If gg is continuous and strictly increasing in each argument, the two classes of defect are indistinguishable to any measurement precision, and no threshold on the score separates them.

Proof. Fix a rule PP with a class CC of size 44, and four foreign elements x1,…,x4x_1, \dots, x_4 all belonging to another class.

Let M1=C∪{x1,x2,x3,x4}M_1 = C \cup \{x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4\}, so |M1|=8|M_1| = 8. Then purity(M1)=4/8=1/2\text{purity}(M_1) = 4/8 = 1/2 and completeness(M1)=4/4=1\text{completeness}(M_1) = 4/4 = 1: impure but complete — the remedy is to remove the four foreign elements.
Let M2={a,b}M_2 = \{a, b\} for two elements a,b∈Ca, b \in C. Then purity(M2)=2/2=1\text{purity}(M_2) = 2/2 = 1 and completeness(M2)=2/4=1/2\text{completeness}(M_2) = 2/4 = 1/2: pure but incomplete — the remedy is to add the two missing members.

Both modules can be realized in one system (E,R,P)(E, R, P).
(a) By symmetry, s(M1)=g(1/2,1)=g(1,1/2)=s(M2)s(M_1) = g(1/2, 1) = g(1, 1/2) = s(M_2): the scores coincide exactly, while the defects and the required repairs are opposite. The geometric mean g(p,c)=pcg(p,c) = \sqrt{pc} scores both modules at 1/21/\sqrt{2}.
(b) Consider the two boundary curves B1={(p,1):0<p<1}B_1 = \{(p, 1) : 0 < p < 1\} (impure-but-complete) and B2={(1,c):0<c<1}B_2 = \{(1, c) : 0 < c < 1\} (pure-but-incomplete). Because gg is strictly increasing, g(1,1)g(1,1) is the supremum of gg on both curves; because gg is continuous, each image g(B1)g(B_1), g(B2)g(B_2) is an interval with that same supremum. Two intervals with a common supremum overlap: there exist (p*,1)∈B1(p^*, 1) \in B_1 and (1,c*)∈B2(1, c^*) \in B_2 with g(p*,1)=g(1,c*)g(p^*, 1) = g(1, c^*). So an impure-but-complete module and a pure-but-incomplete module share the same score, and in their neighbourhood the two classes of module are indistinguishable to any finite precision. An interpretation that reads the failure mode off intervals of the score line therefore misclassifies achievable modules — there is no threshold that separates “remove foreign elements” from “add missing members.” ◼\blacksquare
The single number says something is wrong. It cannot say what, and the two repairs point in opposite directions.

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 4 Failure mode 3 — a number cannot name the element
text:
4 Failure mode 3 — a number cannot name the element
Even a scalar that could read the defect from the score still could not say which element to move. Suppose ss is name-invariant: renaming the elements — carrying one system to another by a bijection σ\sigma with R′=σ(R)R' = \sigma(R), P′=σ∘P∘σ−1P' = \sigma \circ P \circ \sigma^{-1}, ℳ′=σ(ℳ)\mathcal{M}' = \sigma(\mathcal{M}) — leaves the score unchanged, sS′(σ(M))=sS(M)s_{S'}(\sigma(M)) = s_S(M). Any function deserving the name “measurement of the configuration” is name-invariant.

Proposition (no localization). A name-invariant module-level scalar cannot identify the repair target. There are two systems with the same element set, the same module MM, and the same score, whose minimal repairs move different elements.

Proof. Let E={a,b,c,x}E = \{a, b, c, x\}, let R=∅R = \emptyset, and let M={a,b,x}M = \{a, b, x\}.

System 1. P1P_1 induces classes {a,b}\{a, b\} and {c,x}\{c, x\}. Then MM is not a P1P_1-class, and the unique one-move repair is to remove xx: M\{x}={a,b}M \setminus \{x\} = \{a, b\} is a P1P_1-class, while no other single move produces one.
System 2. P2P_2 induces classes {a,x}\{a, x\} and {c,b}\{c, b\}. Again MM is not a class, and the unique one-move repair is to remove bb: M\{b}={a,x}M \setminus \{b\} = \{a, x\}.

Now take the transposition σ=(bx)\sigma = (b\ x), which exchanges bb and xx and fixes aa and cc. It carries system 1 to system 2: σ({a,b})={a,x}\sigma(\{a,b\}) = \{a,x\}, σ({c,x})={c,b}\sigma(\{c,x\}) = \{c,b\}, σ(R)=R\sigma(R) = R, and σ(M)=M\sigma(M) = M (the set {a,b,x}\{a,b,x\} is fixed as a set).
By name-invariance, sS2(M)=sS2(σ(M))=sS1(M)s_{S_2}(M) = s_{S_2}(\sigma(M)) = s_{S_1}(M): the score is the same in both systems. But the repair targets differ — xx in system 1, bb in system 2. A designer observing only the score cannot tell the two configurations apart. And the obstruction is structural, not a matter of resolution: a score fine-grained enough to point at xx rather than bb would have to change under the transposition σ\sigma — and would thereby cease to be name-invariant, that is, cease to measure the configuration. ◼\blacksquare
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 5 Failure mode 4 — a scalar that decides is the rule in disguise
text:
5 Failure mode 4 — a scalar that decides is the rule in disguise
The first three results say a measurement-like scalar fails. The fourth closes the other direction: a scalar that does decide placement adds nothing.

Proposition (degeneracy). Any scalar that decides placement is threshold-equivalent to the rule’s own binary verdict.

Proof. Suppose ss decides placement via dd, in either the element-level form s(e,M)s(e,M) or the module-level form s(M)s(M). Let T={x∈ℝ:d(x)=correct}T = \{x \in \mathbb{R} : d(x) = \text{correct}\}, the preimage of the “correct” verdict. Then, using the definition of the verdict, s(e,M)∈T⇔d(s(e,M))=correct⇔VP(e,M)=correct⇔M=[e]P.
s(e, M) \in T \iff d(s(e,M)) = \text{correct} \iff V_P(e,M) = \text{correct} \iff M = [e]_P .
 So the indicator 1[M=[e]P]1[M = [e]_P] is recovered from the scalar by a single threshold test. (For the module-level form, the same unfolding gives s(M)∈T⇔Ms(M) \in T \iff M is a PP-class, since the verdict is uniform across a module.)
The real-valued structure — magnitude, ordering, continuity, distance from the threshold — contributes nothing to the decision. Any two verdict-deciding scalars induce the same partition of element-module pairs, the partition the rule already defines: one scalar might use [0,1][0,1] with threshold 0.50.5, another ℝ\mathbb{R} with threshold 00, but the partition is identical. ◼\blacksquare
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 6 The four modes cover every scalar
text:
6 The four modes cover every scalar
The results assemble into a trichotomy. Every scalar aimed at the placement verdict either lacks the principle, has it but fails to decide, or decides only degenerately.

Principle-blind. No measurement without PP decides placement (failure mode 1).
Non-deciding. With PP, a scalar may fail to decide. For the measurement-like classes the failure is provable: a scalar factoring through the purity/completeness pair cannot determine the failure mode (failure mode 2), and a name-invariant scalar cannot identify the repair target (failure mode 3).
Degenerate. With PP, any scalar that decides placement is threshold-equivalent to the rule’s binary verdict (failure mode 4).

In every case the placement verdict originates in the partitioning rule, not in a number. A number can repeat the rule’s verdict on a module; only the rule can say what is wrong and which element must move.
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
section: 7 What the scalar is still good for — and what it is not
text:
7 What the scalar is still good for — and what it is not
The result is a limit on deciding. It does not by itself say that a scalar has no practical use — but the usual consolation is weaker than it sounds.
The consolation runs: even if a number cannot decide, it can rank modules for inspection — which to examine first, which grouping looks most suspect. But a ranking asks the scalar to do exactly what the proposition forbids: order modules by comparing an impurity defect with an incompleteness defect on a single line. Any such order presupposes an aggregate g(purity,completeness)g(\text{purity}, \text{completeness}) and, with it, an exchange rate between “an element that does not belong” and “a class member that is missing.” The two axes are independent and incommensurable; nothing in the rule or the domain fixes that rate. Change the aggregate — product, arithmetic mean, weighted sum — and the same modules are ordered differently: a designer ranking by pc\sqrt{pc} and one ranking by 0.7p+0.3c0.7p + 0.3c will name different modules as most suspect, and the rule adjudicates nothing between them.
So even the attention-directing use rests on a convention, not on cohesion. What survives without arbitration is only the degenerate bit: whether a module sits at (1,1)(1,1) or below it — the rule’s own verdict, reproduced by a threshold. Everything finer is a chosen weighting. A scalar score can therefore flag that a module is not a class, and a designer may adopt a heuristic order to decide where to look first — but the order is not grounded in the theory, is not invariant across aggregates, and two defensible scores need not agree.
A separate and weaker point concerns empirical use: structural scores have been reported to correlate with fault-proneness and maintenance effort, so they can serve as screening signals and change predictors. That is a statistical fact about a proxy for change, not a claim that the score measures cohesion — and it does not repair the arbitrariness of ranking by the score.
The impossibility still bites when the score is asked to issue the verdict — to declare an element misplaced from the number alone, without comparing the module against the rule. There, the score is not merely arbitrary; it is the rule in disguise.
crumbs: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric

title: Why Cohesion Has No Scalar Metric
text:
8 Where this comes from
The cohesion schema — correctness relative to a partitioning rule, and the (purity, completeness) pair — is defined and developed in On the Nature of Cohesion [1]. The constructive alternative it points to is the per-rule pair for diagnosis, and the rule PP itself for the verdict. The companion page Why two metrics are necessary proves that the pair is the minimal adequate output for a single rule.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
text: The coupling series supplies what the coupling literature has never had: an ontological account of what coupling is across all its manifestations. Five decades of dimensions, metrics, and measurement frameworks produced no such account. This page collects what the coupling series concludes.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
section: 1 Coupling is access to a shared resource
text:
1 Coupling is access to a shared resource
The central definitional result: two elements are coupled exactly when they access a shared resource.
A resource is anything whose definition, state, or capacity constrains the elements that share it — a module’s interface, a type definition, a database schema, a release pipeline, a team boundary, a deployment unit, a CPU core. A coupling is the ternary relation
(e1,r,e2) (e_1, r, e_2) 
— two entities together with the resource that links them. The resource is the medium of the coupling.
The definition is change-independent: coupling is a standing constraint that holds whether or not any change occurs. Interference and shared fate are couplings that need no change at all.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
section: 2 The recognized dimensions differ only in the resource
text:
2 The recognized dimensions differ only in the resource
Every recognized coupling dimension — structural, temporal, concurrency, semantic, platform — differs only in which resource is shared and how the sharing is enforced. There is no structural difference underneath.
The series provides a taxonomy of resource types organized by seven constraint-kinds (contract, store, medium, budget, authority, location, time) and three coupling modes (definitional, state, capacity). Each coupling dimension maps to its resource, its governing contract, and its enforcement mechanism.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
section: 3 Necessary coupling is to be made manifest, not minimized
text:
3 Necessary coupling is to be made manifest, not minimized
The visibility principle: coupling is not to be minimized but made manifest. Each shared resource is governed by an explicit contract whose violation is immediately detectable.
This reframes the classical imperative. The goal is not to eliminate coupling — coupling is a standing constraint of any system that shares resources — but to make it visible and governed. The directive applies to necessary coupling: the shared-resource edges the system genuinely requires. Accidental coupling is a different target, and it is removed, not merely made visible. The two directives are not in tension because they operate on disjoint edge sets — the visibility principle governs the edges the system needs, while the grouping result below removes the edges above the floor.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
section: 4 Grouping by identical resource-access minimizes accidental coupling
text:
4 Grouping by identical resource-access minimizes accidental coupling
From the coupling definition alone — without change drivers, Γ, or IVP — one result follows: grouping elements by identical resource-access sets
R(e1)=R(e2) R(e_1) = R(e_2) 
minimizes accidental coupling cost.
The series reveals a tripartite structure: E→ℛ→CE \to \mathcal{R} \to C. Every element accesses a set of resources; every resource is governed by a set of change drivers; the element’s change-driver set is derived, not primitive:
Γ(e)=⋃r∈R(e)D(r) \Gamma(e) = \bigcup_{r \in R(e)} D(r) 
This is why the coupling-side and cohesion-side derivations are two ends of the same refinement chain: the resource-set partition refines the Γ partition. Γ is derived from RR through the governance mapping.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
section: 5 Coupling is a consequence of cohesion
text:
5 Coupling is a consequence of cohesion
The classical imperative — “maximize cohesion, minimize coupling” — treats the two as independent objectives requiring a trade-off. The series proves otherwise: within any single dimension, coupling is a consequence of cohesion, and the coupling categories that modularization controls are diagnostic of cohesion defects, not independent design variables.
Coupling decomposes into eight mutually exclusive categories — the product of three binary partitions (internal/external, same-class/cross-class, necessary/not), parameterized by a partitioning rule. At maximal cohesion (purity = completeness = 1), all modularization-controlled coupling categories are empty.
The result: the normative decomposition simultaneously maximizes cohesion and minimizes avoidable coupling — one optimum, not two.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
text:
6 The coupling floor
There is an irreducible coupling the domain demands — the coupling floor. At correct boundaries, the floor equals the necessary dependency graph exactly; every edge above it is a boundary defect or an accidental edge.
Because coupling is measured against a partitioning rule, necessary coupling is rule-relative: the same edge that one concern demands be internal is, under another, demanded external. The imperative to “minimize coupling” has no fixed referent until the rule is fixed. A raw count cannot separate domain-mandated coupling from placement error.

title: Coupling: Core Conclusions
text:
7 Where the proofs live
The proofs — that coupling is access to a shared resource, that the resource-set partition uniquely minimizes accidental coupling, that coupling is a consequence of cohesion, the coupling floor — are in the published coupling papers: the definition of coupling as shared resource access in the paper on the nature of coupling [1], the derivation of the modularisation directive from coupling in the derivation paper [2], and the coupling floor and coupling-as-consequence-of-cohesion results in the decomposition paper [3].


The formal development. The definitions, theorems, and proofs behind this page are published in:

On the Nature of Coupling: All Coupling as Shared Resource Access — Zenodo, 2026 — doi:10.5281/zenodo.21925122
A Self-Contained Derivation of the Optimal Modularization from Coupling — Zenodo, 2026 — doi:10.5281/zenodo.21925268

title: ABAP (7.58)
text:
1 Assessment
This page assesses ABAP in five parts: core coupling — what the language’s own constructs force; ecosystem coupling — what the surrounding platform, tooling, and community cost; engineering readiness — whether the artifact can be reproduced, verified, observed, worked in quickly, connected to other languages, and governed openly; the profile — the unscored facts a score cannot express; and the scoring detail — the mechanism marks and the arithmetic behind every score. A ✅ bullet marks a construct that helps. A ⚠️ or ❌ bullet marks a cost; the scoring model does not price every cost named here.
Core coupling 72.9/100 · Ecosystem coupling 64.5/100 · Engineering readiness 36.8/100

1.1 Core coupling

1.1.1 Type

✅ Static typing is checked at activation: A program is checked against the ABAP Dictionary types before it runs
✅ ABAP Objects gives interfaces and classes: An interface names the methods, and a class implements them without multiple inheritance
✅ The Dictionary is the shared type system: A data element, a domain, or a table type is defined once and referenced by every program
❌ A reference can be unbound: A reference variable starts initial, and the type does not say so; a read without IS BOUND ends the program (T10)
❌ There are no sum types: An alternative is a CASE over a type field or a set of flags, and the compiler does not check that every case is handled (T4)
❌ User code has no generics: A routine that works for many types is written with field symbols or TYPE ANY, which the compiler cannot check (T5)
❌ Run-time type services expose the structure: RTTI reads a type’s components at run time, and ASSIGN COMPONENT reaches a field by name (T7)
⚠️ Two generations share one grammar: A program can mix procedural statements with class-based code in the same include
❌ A call’s effects are not in its type: A signature says what a method returns, not what it writes to the database or the screen (T12)



1.1.2 Construction

✅ A constructor is declared and checked: METHODS constructor runs at CREATE OBJECT, and the class states its own invariants
✅ CREATE OBJECT separates construction from allocation: The runtime allocates, and the class decides what the object holds
⚠️ A class attribute is shared state: A CLASS-DATA attribute is reachable from every caller in the session
❌ Everything is mutable unless declared constant: DATA is the default and CONSTANTS is opt-in, so an object’s fields can change under a holder (C2)
❌ Execution moves with no call in sight: dynamic method invocation (CALL METHOD (name)) and dynamic attribute access run the code a string names, not a call site (C7)



1.1.3 Memory

✅ The runtime manages memory: Objects and internal tables are released by the ABAP runtime, and a program never frees storage by hand
✅ An internal table is the collection type: A table is a typed container the runtime manages, and an index read is bounds-checked
⚠️ No destructor runs at scope exit: A lock, a file, or a cursor is released by the logical unit of work or by an explicit close
⚠️ A large internal table lives in the session’s memory: The runtime’s memory is bounded per work process, and a big table is a sizing decision
❌ The undeclared class has no catch: a runtime error dumps the internal session (documented), below the CATCH cx_ surface (Er6)



1.1.4 Error

❌ Class-based exceptions are declared but not enforced: A method can raise CX_*, and a caller is not required to handle it; a run-time error ends the program (Er2)
❌ There is no result type: A failure travels as an exception or as sy-subrc, and neither composes (Er4)
❌ sy-subrc can be ignored: The classic return code is set by a statement, and nothing forces the next statement to read it (Er3)
✅ TRY ... CATCH ... CLEANUP gives a structured path: A class-based exception is caught by type, and CLEANUP runs on the way out



1.1.5 Concurrency

✅ A function module can start a new task: CALL FUNCTION ... STARTING NEW TASK runs a unit in parallel, and RECEIVE RESULTS collects it
❌ Shared state is the default across sessions: A database row, a shared memory area, or a lock object is reachable from every session, and nothing in the type marks it (K2)
✅ A lock object states the protocol: An ENQUEUE/DEQUEUE pair names the object it protects, so the lock is a repository object
⚠️ The unit of work is the transaction: A logical unit of work commits or rolls back as a whole, and a long dialog step holds it open



1.1.6 Platform

❌ A program runs only inside an SAP system: The ABAP runtime, the Dictionary, and the database interface are the platform, and there is no other host (P1)
✅ The database is abstracted: Open SQL is translated by the database interface, so one program runs on HANA, Db2, Oracle, or SQL Server
✅ The kernel is the virtual machine: The runtime executes the generated code and controls screens, events, and the database interface
⚠️ The cloud flavour restricts the language: ABAP for Cloud Development permits a subset, so an on-premise program may not be allowed in the cloud
❌ Ordinary application work is expensive: There is no general file, socket, or thread API in the language, so a task outside the business model is built from the runtime’s interfaces (P4)



1.1.7 Trade-offs (not coupling)

Vendor lock-in is the price of the platform: The Dictionary, the transport system, and the runtime are one product
Compatibility is kept at the cost of consistency: Every generation of syntax remains valid, so two idioms coexist indefinitely
The deployment unit is a transport, not a build: A program is activated in a system, so the artifact cannot be rebuilt from source alone
The business model is the language’s domain: A data model is expressed in the Dictionary, and a task outside it needs the runtime’s interfaces
The tooling is integrated and closed: ADT and the transport system are strong inside SAP and unavailable outside it




1.2 Ecosystem coupling

1.2.1 Performance

❌ A program is interpreted from generated code: The kernel executes the generated form, and there is no ahead-of-time path to machine code (R1)
✅ Code pushdown moves work to the database: CDS views and Open SQL carry the set operation to the database instead of looping in ABAP
⚠️ A nested loop over two internal tables is the classic cost: The code-pushdown guidance exists to replace that pattern
✅ Buffering holds hot data in the application server: A table buffer keeps frequently read data in the server’s memory



1.2.2 Ecosystem

❌ The ecosystem belongs to one vendor: SAP ships the language, the runtime, the tooling, and the applications, and no third party can implement ABAP (Ec4)
❌ One runtime and one framework dominate: The SAP programming model, the Dictionary, and the transport system are the only route (Ec6)
❌ Decades of code remain in the repository: A release keeps old syntax, old APIs, and old idioms working, so every new feature coexists with them (Ec7)
✅ ABAP Development Tools is a capable IDE: Eclipse-based editing, syntax check, debugging, and transport are integrated
✅ abapGit brings version control: A repository can be exported to Git, so a team can review changes outside the transport system



1.2.3 Evolution

✅ The compatibility promise is strong: A release keeps old statements working, so an upgrade rarely breaks a program
✅ New syntax is additive: Inline declarations, constructor expressions, and CDS arrived without invalidating older code
⚠️ The repository accumulates every generation: A system carries classic reports, function modules, and classes side by side
⚠️ The language level moves with the platform: A program’s language level changes when the system is upgraded, not on the program’s schedule



1.2.4 Domain

❌ The domain is enterprise business software: A program models orders, invoices, and materials inside an ERP system (D1)
❌ The framework sets the architecture: The dynpro or RESTful Application Programming model, the logical unit of work, and the package hierarchy decide the program’s structure (D3)
✅ The Dictionary and CDS model the data: A business entity is defined once and used by reports, services, and the UI



1.2.5 Learning

❌ The language and the platform are learned together: A newcomer learns the syntax, the Dictionary, the transport system, and the business model at once (L1)
❌ The surface is large: Classic procedural syntax, ABAP Objects, CDS, and the RAP framework are four vocabularies (L2)
✅ The documentation is exhaustive: SAP’s keyword documentation covers the language in detail



1.2.6 Syntax

❌ The syntax is sentence-like and verbose: DATA, TYPE, and WRITE spell out what a C-family language infers from punctuation (S1)
❌ Two generations share one grammar: Procedural statements and class-based expressions coexist, and either style can appear in one program (S2)
✅ Constructor expressions are modern: NEW, VALUE, COND, and SWITCH express a value where older code assigned it



1.2.7 Testing

✅ ABAP Unit runs inside the system: A test class is a repository object, and the runner reports in the same session
✅ The debugger is strong: A program is stepped, a variable is watched, and a run-time error is analysed in the same session
✅ ATC checks against a rule set: The ABAP Test Cockpit applies the rules at transport time
⚠️ A test needs a system: There is no local build and test loop; the test runs in a system with its data



1.2.8 Security

✅ Memory is managed: A program cannot read or write outside its data, and a table read is bounds-checked
✅ The authorization concept is part of the platform: An authority check names the object and the field, and the runtime enforces it
❌ Dynamic SQL and dynamic calls are ordinary statements: A WHERE clause or a method name can be built from a string, so concatenated input is an injection path (Q3)
⚠️ A modification is the risk surface: A change to a standard object must be re-applied at every upgrade

1.3 Engineering readiness

1.3.1 Reproducibility

❌ The artifact is transported, not built: A program is activated in a system, so the deployed object depends on that system’s state and cannot be rebuilt from source alone (Y1)
❌ Dependencies are a system level, not a manifest: A program relies on the SAP_BASIS release and on repository objects, and nothing in the source pins them (Y2)



1.3.2 Supply chain

❌ A transport carries no signature: The import queue moves objects between systems on trust, and a receiver cannot verify who produced them (Y3)



1.3.3 Observability

❌ Trace and statistics are vendor tools: ST05, SAT, and the ABAP trace are the analysis path, and no open tracing standard is built in (Y5)
❌ Logging is a framework API: The application log is a class library, not a language facility, and a program can write nothing at all (Y6)



1.3.4 Feedback

✅ The syntax check is immediate: ADT checks a class or a program in the system, so an error is reported without a build



1.3.5 Interop

❌ There is no portable target: The generated code runs only in the ABAP runtime, and a program cannot be shipped to another platform (Y10)



1.3.6 Governance

❌ One vendor governs the language: SAP defines the syntax, the runtime, and the release schedule, and no independent body ratifies a change (Y11)
❌ The specification is a vendor document: The keyword documentation is authoritative and proprietary, and no public standard defines ABAP (Y12)
❌ Semantics rest on the vendor runtime: the keyword documentation defines the language as the vendor’s runtime behaves, and no published conformance suite exists (Y17)
❌ No parser published: the keyword documentation defines the surface, the kernel’s parser is closed, and no parser API ships (Y19)




1.4 Profile
Unscored, and kept separate from every score on purpose. The profile records what a mechanism price cannot express: what a running program costs, how well a coding model and an agent work in the language, and whether a safety-critical path exists.

1.4.1 Energy and cost
What this axis asks: what does a running program cost in energy and time?

⚠️ Runs on the SAP application server; no independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.



1.4.2 AI and agent readiness
What this axis asks: how well does a coding model and an agent work in this language?

❌ Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [5].



1.4.3 Safety certification
What this axis asks: is there a certified or standards-qualified path to a safety-critical system?

⚠️ No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

Verdict: ABAP’s design yields high language-imposed coupling. The runtime, the Dictionary, and the vendor own the platform, so the deployment unit is one product. Static typing, ABAP Objects, and managed memory remove several language mechanisms, but the classic return code, the untyped dynamic SQL, the mutable-by-default data, and the absence of a result type keep the error and construction paths open. Main strength: a mature, strongly typed business language with a managed runtime and a strong compatibility promise. Main weakness: a program runs only inside an SAP system, the framework decides the architecture, and the repository carries every generation of the language at once.

title: Clojure (1.12)
text:
1 Assessment
This page assesses Clojure in five parts: core coupling — what the language’s own constructs force; ecosystem coupling — what the surrounding platform, tooling, and community cost; engineering readiness — whether the artifact can be reproduced, verified, observed, worked in quickly, connected to other languages, and governed openly; the profile — the unscored facts a score cannot express; and the scoring detail — the mechanism marks and the arithmetic behind every score. A ✅ bullet marks a construct that helps. A ⚠️ or ❌ bullet marks a cost; the scoring model does not price every cost named here.
Core coupling 74.0/100 · Ecosystem coupling 89.1/100 · Engineering readiness 67.8/100

1.1 Core coupling

1.1.1 Type

✅ Protocols decouple behaviour from inheritance: defprotocol declares a set of functions, and extend-type and extend-protocol implement them for any type, including Java classes and nil, so behaviour is added without a class hierarchy
❌ Dynamic typing defers every type check to run time: A function declares no parameter or return type, so a mismatch is found when the value is used (T1)
❌ Protocol dispatch resolves at run time: The implementation is chosen from the value’s type when the call executes, and a type with no implementation fails then (T3)
❌ No sum types and no generics: Alternatives are tagged maps or :type keywords by convention, and a function accepts any value, so neither the case set nor the argument shape is checked by the compiler (T4, T5)
⚠️ Operator names are ordinary vars: + and = can be shadowed in a namespace or a local binding, so a reader resolves the symbol from the current scope (T8)
✅ clojure.spec checks a boundary on demand: A spec declares the shape of arguments and results, and instrument turns it into a run-time assertion where a program chooses to
❌ Inherits the JVM answer: string length counts UTF-16 units (T15)



1.1.2 Construction

✅ Immutable structures decouple a change from its readers: assoc, conj, and update return a new value and leave the old one intact, so a reader that holds the earlier value sees no change
✅ Persistent structures share their unchanged parts: A vector, map, or set update copies only the changed path, so immutability does not cost a full copy
✅ let scopes a binding to its form: A value’s lifetime is its lexical form, so construction does not depend on a declaration elsewhere
✅ Records separate data from behaviour: defrecord gives an associative value with named fields, and plain functions operate on it without a class that owns them
✅ Macros extend the surface syntax without changing the core: defmacro transforms forms at compile time, so a domain notation is added outside the language
⚠️ Top-level def state is globally visible: A def or defonce var is reachable from every namespace, and alter-var-root can rebind it, so shared state needs discipline
❌ Collection order is unpinned: past eight entries a map literal becomes a hashed map, so the traversal the source sees changes with the data (C5)



1.1.3 Memory

❌ The JVM garbage collector pauses the program: Reclamation timing is the collector’s decision, so a latency-sensitive path cannot assume a bound (M2)
❌ No RAII: Destruction is not tied to scope, and finalize and java.lang.ref.Cleaner are unreliable, so release must be explicit (M3)
❌ No ownership model: A value can be referenced from anywhere on the heap, and the collector reclaims it only after the last reference disappears (M4)
✅ Immutable values make sharing safe: Because a value cannot change in place, handing the same reference to another thread cannot alter the first holder’s view
✅ with-open releases a resource at scope exit: The macro expands to try/finally, so a file, socket, or stream is closed even on an exception
✅ Direct buffers keep bulk data off the managed heap: java.nio.ByteBuffer.allocateDirect and primitive arrays reduce collector pressure on large payloads



1.1.4 Error

❌ Exceptions are unchecked: A JVM exception propagates without declaration, so a function’s failure set is not visible in its signature (Er2)
✅ ex-info carries a data map: ex-info attaches a map that ex-data reads, so a handler inspects structured context instead of parsing a message
✅ try/catch/finally separates the recovery path: Recovery code sits in a dedicated form beside the normal path
✅ Function preconditions and postconditions are declarative: :pre and :post in a defn attribute map check a call and its result at run time
⚠️ A failure surfaces only when the value is used: With no declared types there is no compile-time list of what a call can raise



1.1.5 Concurrency

✅ Immutable data is the default: A value shared between threads cannot be changed by another thread, so most data needs no lock
✅ Atoms give uncoordinated synchronous change: swap! updates one reference with compare-and-set semantics and reset! stores a value outright, independent of every other reference
✅ Refs and dosync give coordinated STM transactions: alter inside a transaction commits all its references atomically or retries, so a multi-reference change is isolated and composable
✅ Agents give asynchronous serialised updates: send and send-off queue an action, and each agent runs its actions in order
✅ core.async channels decouple producers from consumers: chan and go blocks transfer values without shared mutable state
⚠️ A transaction can retry its body: A conflicting dosync block runs again, so a side effect inside it may happen more than once



1.1.6 Platform

✅ Full access to the JVM ecosystem: import, proxy, and gen-class let Clojure call any Java library directly
✅ ClojureScript compiles the same language to JavaScript: The Google Closure compiler targets the browser and Node.js from the same source
✅ .cljc reader conditionals share code across hosts: One file selects host-specific forms at read time, so common logic stays in one place
⚠️ JVM start-up precedes main: A command-line run pays the JVM initialisation cost before the program executes
⚠️ Host interop couples a namespace to its host: A namespace that imports java.util.Date cannot run on ClojureScript unless the host-specific parts are isolated



1.1.7 Trade-offs (not coupling)

Dynamic typing is a deliberate trade: No declarations speed construction and suit a REPL-first workflow, at the cost of run-time type checking
Lisp syntax is the price of homoiconicity: Parentheses and prefix notation buy code-as-data, which is what macros need
Simple versus easy is a design value: Hickey’s distinction favours composable values over convenient wrappers, and that choice shapes the standard library rather than forcing a dependency
A hosted language inherits its host’s trade-offs: JVM start-up and collection come from the platform choice, not from a mechanism of the language
REPL-driven development assumes a running image: The workflow favours exploration and interactive work, which is a team scope decision
Clojure is not a systems language: It assumes a host VM and a collector, which is a scope boundary rather than a defect




1.2 Ecosystem coupling

1.2.1 Performance

⚠️ JIT warm-up precedes peak speed: HotSpot interprets first and compiles hot paths later, so a short-lived process may never reach peak throughput (R3)
✅ Hot paths reach native speed: On a long-running service the JIT compiles the hot loops to machine code
✅ Persistent structures keep update cost logarithmic: An update shares the unchanged parts, so immutability does not multiply allocation
✅ Transients build a collection in place: transient and persistent! construct a large collection without intermediate copies where it is not yet shared
⚠️ Boxing and reflection cost throughput: Untyped arithmetic boxes numbers, and a reflective Java call resolves at run time unless a type hint (^) is present
⚠️ Start-up is slow: JVM initialisation and namespace loading make a short command-line program slower than a native binary



1.2.2 Ecosystem

❌ The library base is small beside Java and npm: The number of available libraries is a fraction of those ecosystems (Ec3)
✅ The whole JVM library base is reachable: A deps.edn or Leiningen project resolves Maven artifacts, so Java libraries are used directly
✅ Clojars and Maven give dependency management: Resolution, versioning, and publishing are tooled and reproducible
✅ The core library is small and deliberate: clojure.core is stable and rarely needs a breaking change
⚠️ Build conventions differ between teams: Leiningen, deps.edn/tools.deps, and babashka coexist, so project layouts vary
✅ The class file carries a published promise: Clojure reaches consumers as JVM bytecode [5] (Ec8)
✅ Serialized objects cross on a published promise: the stream carries the format version and a per-class serial version UID, and the specification states the current protocol is fully backward and forward compatible, read by JDK 1.1.7 and later [6] (Ec9)



1.2.3 Evolution

✅ The core language changes conservatively: New capability usually arrives as a library, so clojure.core stays stable
✅ Old code keeps running: Releases add functions and rarely remove or change existing behaviour
✅ Reader conditionals support one source for several hosts: A .cljc file keeps shared code current across Clojure and ClojureScript
⚠️ A new JDK is a platform event: Running on a newer Java release follows the JVM’s schedule, not Clojure’s
❌ Build variants multiply: reader conditionals (#?(:clj … :cljs …)) select which forms read for each target (V7)



1.2.4 Domain

✅ Excellent for web services: Ring, Compojure, and Reitit express HTTP handling in plain functions and data
✅ Excellent for data processing: Transducers and core.async pipelines process sequences and streams without intermediate collections
✅ The REPL suits exploratory and interactive work: The running image allows a function to be redefined and retried immediately
✅ ClojureScript reaches the browser: One language covers frontend and backend
⚠️ Less common for systems and numeric work: No native memory control and no static numeric types make it unusual for kernels and HPC



1.2.5 Learning

❌ The learning curve is steep: It combines Lisp syntax, functional programming, and JVM integration in one language (L1)
✅ The core is small and consistent: clojure.core fits in a reference page, and one data model applies everywhere
✅ The REPL gives immediate feedback: A form is evaluated at once and its value is visible
⚠️ Macro writing is a second step: Understanding expansion and hygiene takes practice beyond ordinary functions
⚠️ Stack traces cross into the JVM: A failure reports Java frames and reader positions together



1.2.6 Syntax

✅ Parenthesised forms are uniform: Code and data share the S-expression representation, so there is no grammar beyond lists
✅ Prefix notation removes precedence rules: (+ 1 2) puts the operator first everywhere
✅ Few special forms: let, fn, def, if, do, and quote cover most of the core
⚠️ Delimiters are dense: Deep nesting is hard to read without an editor that matches parentheses
⚠️ Threading and reader macros add notation: ->, ->>, #(), and @ are terse and must be learned



1.2.7 Testing

✅ clojure.test is in the core library: deftest, is, and testing need no external dependency
✅ A test runs against the live image: Code can be redefined and a test re-run without a restart
✅ clojure.spec supports generative testing: clojure.spec.test.alpha/check generates inputs from a spec and validates the results
⚠️ No compiler check finds a broken call site: With dynamic typing the test suite, not the compiler, catches it



1.2.8 Security

✅ Immutability limits accidental sharing: A value cannot be mutated behind another holder’s back
✅ No unsafe memory access in the language: Clojure code cannot forge a pointer, and the JVM verifies bytecode
✅ The JVM’s process and sandbox model applies: A program runs under the host VM’s isolation
⚠️ eval of constructed data is code execution: clojure.core/read-string can run reader macros, so untrusted input must not reach read or eval
⚠️ A boundary check helps only where it is enabled: A spec check runs when the program instruments or validates, not automatically

1.3 Engineering readiness

1.3.1 Reproducibility

❌ A build resolves the dependency graph at run time through the REPL and the classpath. (Y1)
❌ tools.deps resolves versions from the manifest unless the deps.edn pins them. (Y2)



1.3.2 Supply chain

❌ Maven Central is one flat name space for the jars the classpath resolves. (Y4)
⚠️ Clojure ships no package channel; Maven Central and git deps are the ecosystem’s.



1.3.3 Observability

❌ No tracing standard exists in the language; JVM tooling observes the artifact. (Y5)



1.3.4 Feedback

❌ No debugger ships with the toolchain; the REPL is the diagnostic surface. (Y13)



1.3.5 Interop

❌ The maintained target is the host JVM; ClojureScript and Babashka trail the compiler. (Y10)



1.3.6 Governance

❌ Semantics rest on the reference implementation: the language is documented as the behavior of the reference implementation, and no published conformance suite exists (Y17)




1.4 Profile
Unscored, and kept separate from every score on purpose. The profile records what a mechanism price cannot express: what a running program costs, how well a coding model and an agent work in the language, and whether a safety-critical path exists.

1.4.1 Energy and cost
What this axis asks: what does a running program cost in energy and time?

⚠️ Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [7]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [8].



1.4.2 AI and agent readiness
What this axis asks: how well does a coding model and an agent work in this language?

⚠️ Moderate training data: models write it competently, with measurable language-specific weakness [9].



1.4.3 Safety certification
What this axis asks: is there a certified or standards-qualified path to a safety-critical system?

⚠️ No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

Verdict: Clojure removes a large class of coupling in its own constructs: immutable values by default, protocols that add behaviour without a class hierarchy, atoms, refs, and agents for the three coordination styles, STM for coordinated change, and macros for extending syntax. Core coupling stays moderate because typing is dynamic, so a mismatch is caught at run time rather than at compile time, and because every value lives on a JVM heap with a collector. The platform and ecosystem dimension is the stronger half: full access to the JVM library base, a stable core, and ClojureScript for the browser, at the cost of JVM start-up, a library base smaller than Java’s, and a steep combination of Lisp syntax, functional style, and JVM integration.

title: C# (13)
text:
1 Assessment
This page assesses C# in five parts: core coupling — what the language’s own constructs force; ecosystem coupling — what the surrounding platform, tooling, and community cost; engineering readiness — whether the artifact can be reproduced, verified, observed, worked in quickly, connected to other languages, and governed openly; the profile — the unscored facts a score cannot express; and the scoring detail — the mechanism marks and the arithmetic behind every score. A ✅ bullet marks a construct that helps. A ⚠️ or ❌ bullet marks a cost; the scoring model does not price every cost named here.
Core coupling 65.7/100 · Ecosystem coupling 72.3/100 · Engineering readiness 88.3/100

1.1 Core coupling

1.1.1 Type

✅ Interfaces + extension methods: Can add behavior without coupling to classes
✅ Generics with constraints: Better than Java (no erasure, value type generics)
✅ LINQ separates iteration from logic: Query syntax decouples data operations
⚠️ Inheritance still available: Can couple via class hierarchies
✅ Nullable reference types (C# 8+): Separates nullable from non-nullable
✅ File-scoped types (C# 11): file access modifier restricts visibility to a source file, tightening encapsulation
❌ Null still exists alongside nullable types: Migration incomplete
❌ Properties can have side effects: obj.Prop might do anything
⚠️ .NET runtime allows reflection: Can break encapsulation
❌ Char is documented as a UTF-16 code unit; String.Length counts units (T15)



1.1.2 Construction

✅ Object initializers decouple: new Person { Name = "Alice", Age = 30 }
✅ Records (C# 9+) are immutable: Value semantics prevent coupling
✅ Primary constructors (C# 12): Reduce construction boilerplate on class/struct
✅ Collection expressions (C# 12): [1, 2, 3] unified syntax decouples creation from collection type
⚠️ Constructors can have side effects: No enforcement of pure construction
✅ DI built into ASP.NET Core: Framework-level construction decoupling
❌ Static state couples: Singleton patterns common
❌ Collection order is unpinned: the documentation warns that Dictionary iteration order must not be relied on, and the ordered collections are opt-in (C5)
❌ One value, many names: class instances move by reference, a field, a parameter, and a lambda share one object, and no declaration names the alias set (readonly is a discipline on the field, not the graph) (C6)
❌ Execution moves with no call in sight: user-defined implicit conversion operators run at assignment and argument sites (C7)
❌ ECMA-335 declares the order in which static constructors run unpredictable (C8)



1.1.3 Memory

✅ .NET GC decouples memory: Generational GC (gen0, gen1, gen2, LOH)
✅ No manual memory management for managed code: Safe by default
⚠️ GC pauses affect latency: Server/workstation GC modes, background GC helps
✅ IDisposable pattern for resources: Deterministic cleanup via using statement
⚠️ Finalizers couple cleanup to GC: Non-deterministic timing
⚠️ Stack-allocated structs: Value types avoid GC but couple to stack lifetime
✅ Span reduces allocations: Stack-based memory without GC pressure
✅ The class is declared: OutOfMemoryException carries a documented contract (the runtime restores the process after a heap failure) and is catchable (Er6)



1.1.4 Error

❌ Unchecked exceptions: No throws clause, errors hidden
⚠️ Result types uncommon: Libraries exist (LanguageExt) but not idiomatic
✅ Nullable pattern helps: ?. operator reduces null coupling
❌ A fault ends the process: an unhandled exception in any thread terminates the process (documented); try/catch recovers in the frame, and no unit is declared (Er5)



1.1.5 Concurrency

✅ Async/await excellent: Best async syntax in mainstream languages
✅ Task separates async: Clear distinction from sync code
✅ Lock type (C# 13): Dedicated System.Threading.Lock with pattern-based using scoping — decouples synchronization from object casting
❌ Can still use threads with shared state: Traditional coupling available
✅ Immutable collections available: System.Collections.Immutable, FrozenSet/FrozenDictionary (C# 12+) prevent concurrent coupling with zero overhead



1.1.6 Platform

✅ Open-source runtime and compiler: .NET is MIT licensed, and the Roslyn compiler is developed in the open
✅ Cross-platform runtime: The same compiled library runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, and WebAssembly (Blazor)
✅ Multiple implementations: CoreCLR, Mono, and .NET Framework each run C# code, so the language is not bound to one runtime
✅ No runtime version lock-in: Side-by-side runtime versions let an application pin its own .NET version



1.1.7 Trade-offs (not coupling)

async colours a method: The modifier changes what its callers must do, so synchronous and asynchronous code do not compose freely — a deliberate trade
Nullability checking is a project setting: <Nullable>enable</Nullable> turns the checks on per project, so adoption is incremental — a migration choice, not a forced dependency
Unsafe code stays in the language: Pointers, P/Invoke, and COM are available for what the managed runtime cannot serve, a deliberate escape hatch rather than a dependency
Two runtimes share the language: Code that must also run on .NET Framework limits itself to the common subset — a compatibility trade, not a coupling
Code generation is part of the build: Source generators and partial types let tooling contribute half of a class, which moves work into the compilation step




1.2 Ecosystem coupling

1.2.1 Performance

✅ Excellent JIT optimization: CLR is highly optimized
⚠️ GC pauses: Server and background modes bound the pause but do not remove it, and the collector decides when it runs (R2)
✅ Tunable GC: Multiple GC modes for different scenarios
✅ Span/Memory: Zero-copy optimizations decouple performance from allocations
⚠️ Startup time: JIT warmup (mitigated by ReadyToRun)
✅ Native AOT: Recent addition decouples from JIT



1.2.2 Ecosystem

✅ Massive .NET ecosystem: NuGet has everything
⚠️ Framework monoculture: ASP.NET Core and the Microsoft stack dominate, so the alternatives are not really alternatives (Ec6)
✅ Excellent tooling: Visual Studio, Rider, VSCode
✅ dotnet CLI: Standardized, consistent
✅ Cross-platform: .NET runs everywhere
✅ Great IDE support: IntelliSense, refactoring
✅ CLR metadata carries a published promise: IL assemblies follow a standardised format, and the runtime publishes its compatibility rules [5], [6] (Ec8)
❌ Stored payloads bind to the runtime: Microsoft states that BinaryFormatter throws NotSupportedException across nearly all project types from .NET 8, and that .NET 9 removed the in-box implementation and the settings that enabled it, so a payload written on an older runtime no longer has a reader [7], [8] (Ec9)



1.2.3 Evolution

✅ Excellent backward compatibility: Rarely breaks
✅ Rapid innovation: New features every year
✅ Nullable reference types: Opt-in migration
✅ Modern features: Records, pattern matching, LINQ
❌ Build variants multiply: #if blocks with DefineConstants select which members compile, and the flag set lives in the project file, not the source (V7)



1.2.4 Domain

✅ Excellent for backend: ASP.NET industry standard
✅ Great for desktop: WPF, WinForms, Avalonia
✅ Strong for games: Unity uses C#
✅ Good for mobile: Xamarin/MAUI
⚠️ Web frontend: Blazor exists but less common



1.2.5 Learning

✅ Gentle: Similar to Java, well-documented
✅ Excellent docs: Microsoft docs are comprehensive
⚠️ Many features: LINQ, async, delegates can overwhelm
✅ Good tutorials: Lots of learning resources



1.2.6 Syntax

✅ Less verbose than Java: Properties, expression bodies
✅ LINQ syntax: Expressive, decouples queries
⚠️ Type inference limited: Often need explicit types
✅ Modern features: Pattern matching, records reduce boilerplate



1.2.7 Testing

✅ xUnit, NUnit, MSTest: Mature frameworks
✅ World-class debugger: Visual Studio debugger is best-in-class
✅ Profiling tools: dotTrace, PerfView
✅ Hot reload: Edit and continue



1.2.8 Security

✅ Memory safe: GC prevents memory bugs
✅ Type safe: Strong static typing
✅ Nullable reference types: Eliminates many null bugs
⚠️ Unsafe code: unsafe keyword bypasses safety
⚠️ Serialization issues: JSON/XML vulnerabilities
❌ The default unchecked arithmetic wraps Int32/Int64 in two’s complement; checked is the opt-in, a mitigation (Q4)

1.3.1 Reproducibility

❌ Package versions resolve from NuGet unless the restore pins them. (Y2)
✅ The project file and global.json are contracts the SDK reads and validates. (Y18)



1.3.2 Supply chain

❌ The nuget.org name space is flat. (Y4)
⚠️ The GitHub advisory database covers NuGet packages, not the registry itself.



1.3.3 Observability

✅ System.Diagnostics.Metrics and Activity ship in the base class library. (Y5)
✅ ILogger is the structured logging contract the platform ships. (Y6)
✅ Crash dumps and platform error reporting ship by default. (Y15)



1.3.4 Feedback

❌ No debugger ships with the SDK; the IDE debuggers are separate installs. (Y13)



1.3.5 Interop

✅ P/Invoke is the in-process C interface, with NativeAOT for static linking. (Y9)
✅ The runtime ships maintained builds for the common platforms. (Y10)



1.3.6 Governance

✅ The .NET Foundation stewards the language; the RFC process is public. (Y11)
✅ ECMA-334 and ISO/IEC 23271 publish the standards. (Y12)
✅ The CLI conformance suite backs the language standard. (Y17)
✅ Roslyn and the runtime are public source. (Y19)




1.4 Profile
Unscored, and kept separate from every score on purpose. The profile records what a mechanism price cannot express: what a running program costs, how well a coding model and an agent work in the language, and whether a safety-critical path exists.

1.4.1 Energy and cost
What this axis asks: what does a running program cost in energy and time?

⚠️ Runs on a virtual machine, above native code in the energy and time benchmarks [9]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [10].



1.4.2 AI and agent readiness
What this axis asks: how well does a coding model and an agent work in this language?

✅ A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [11], [12].

What this axis asks: is there a certified or standards-qualified path to a safety-critical system?

⚠️ No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
